h1: Rodent Proofing in San Leandro, CA
description: Rodent proofing in San Leandro, CA: seal the entry points rats and mice use so they stay out for good. Get a free inspection and estimate.
intro: Rodent proofing for East Bay homes: we find and seal the entry points rats and mice use, so they never get inside in the first place. Free inspection of the roof line, vents, penetrations and access points.
hero_alt: Sealing a roof gap against rodents in San Leandro

sections.h2: How rodents get into East Bay homes
paragraphs: Rats and mice need an opening no wider than a dime in some cases. Roof gaps, vent openings, pipe penetrations and the junctions where roofs meet walls are all doors for them.
Proofing finds those openings before rodents do and closes them with materials they cannot chew through.
bullets: Gaps where walls meet the roof

sections.h2: Sealing the entry points that matter
paragraphs: We work from the outside in: every roof-to-wall junction, vent, penetration and gap gets checked, then sealed with metal flashing, hardware cloth or foam rated for the job.
bullets: Metal flashing over wide roof gaps
Hardware cloth on vents and louvers
Sealant and foam on small penetrations
Access points checked on every side of the house

paragraphs: Traps remove individual rodents but leave the door open for the next ones. Proofing closes the building so the problem ends instead of repeating.
Proofing is also what protects new insulation: fresh material in a rodent-accessible attic is just future nesting.
If you are planning attic insulation, proofing should happen first. We seal the openings, then the insulation goes in, so you are not paying to insulate a rodent highway.
The inspection looks at both jobs together and quotes them in the right order.
Proofing is a one-time fix on the structure, not an ongoing service. We seal the openings, document what was closed with photos, and point out the spots to watch seasonally.
If rodents have already been inside, we can add the cleanup and reinsulation scope so the attic is fully restored.

steps.name: Inspection
steps.text: We walk the roof line, vents, penetrations and the garage to map every opening a rodent could use.

faqs.q: How do rodents get into the attic?
faqs.a: Through roof gaps, vent openings, pipe penetrations and the junctions where walls meet the roof. Most openings are small enough to miss until someone looks for them.

faqs.q: Does proofing work if rodents are already inside?
faqs.a: Proofing closes the building so no new ones enter. If rodents are already inside, we add exclusion and cleanup so the problem is fully resolved, not just walled in.
Metal flashing and hardware cloth for the openings rodents chew through, plus sealants and foam for small penetrations. Nothing gets sealed with a material they can reopen.
A typical house takes a day. Homes with many openings or difficult roof access can run longer, and the estimate states the schedule.

faqs.q: Should I proof before insulating my attic?
faqs.a: Yes. Sealing the entry points first is what keeps new insulation clean and dry. We quote both jobs together in the right order.

faqs.q: Will proofing affect my roof ventilation?
faqs.a: No. Vents are screened, not blocked, so airflow continues while rodents stay out.
